text_blocks.snippet: San Francisco offers a mix of iconic landmarks, distinct neighborhoods, and scenic waterfronts. Top must-see spots include the legendary Golden Gate Bridge, the notorious former prison on Alcatraz Island, and the vibrant, bustling piers of Fisherman's Wharf.
snippet_highlighted_words: Golden Gate Bridge, the notorious former prison on Alcatraz Island, and the vibrant, bustling piers of Fisherman's Wharf

text_blocks.snippet: Explore these top areas to experience the best of the city:

list.snippet: Golden Gate Bridge: Walk or bike across the span for sweeping views of the bay, or head to Battery Spencer in the Marin Headlands for the perfect postcard picture.
Alcatraz Island: Take a short ferry ride to "The Rock" and explore the legendary penitentiary with an immersive audio tour. (Book tickets in advance!)
Golden Gate Park: This massive urban oasis is larger than NYC's Central Park. Highlights include the Japanese Tea Garden and the Conservatory of Flowers.
Palace of Fine Arts: A stunning, Greco-Roman architectural structure complete with a serene lagoon and sweeping rotunda.
Lombard Street: Known as the "crookedest street in the world," this winding, beautifully landscaped road features eight sharp hairpin turns.
Chinatown: Wander through the oldest Chinatown in North America. Be sure to explore the vibrant side streets and visit the famous Golden Gate Fortune Cookie Factory.
The Painted Ladies: Located across from Alamo Square Park, this iconic row of colorful Victorian houses is famous for its backdrop of the modern city skyline.
Haight-Ashbury: The birthplace of the 1960s hippie counterculture, this area is now a vibrant strip packed with excellent vintage clothing shops, bookstores, and record stores.
Ferry Building: Located on the Embarcadero, this public food lover's paradise features artisanal cheese shops, local coffee roasters, and bakeries.
Fisherman’s Wharf & Pier 39: While undeniably touristy, it offers unbeatable clam chowder, fun vintage arcades like the Musée Mécanique, and the famous sunbathing sea lions.

Coit Tower: Drive or walk up Telegraph Hill to this art deco tower, which features historic murals at its base and a 360-degree observation deck offering panoramic views of the city skyline and the bay.
